purpose: watch the servers, containers, clusters and cloud services under the applications, so saturation and failure are found early and tied to their cause
entry_criteria: Agents or exporters can be deployed
procedure: Collect host and container metrics: CPU including steal and throttling, memory and swap, disk space, inode and I/O latency, network errors and saturation.
Collect orchestrator signals: pod restarts, pending pods, node conditions, resource requests and limits, and autoscaler activity.
Collect cloud service metrics and quota use for managed services, and alert before quotas are reached.
Alert on saturation trends and time-to-full forecasts, such as disks that will fill within a day, rather than only on current values.
Tag metrics with service, environment and owner, so alerts route to the right team and show affected applications.
Test that monitoring itself works: alert on missing data from the agents and on failure of the monitoring pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Every host and cluster reports metrics
worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: A forecast alert warns that a database volume fills in 18 hours at the current growth; the team expands it during working hours, and a test shows the absent-data alert fires when an exporter is stopped.
